messages.body_plain:

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Sleep variables for day time sleep
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Sleep variables for day time sleep
messages.body_plain:
In the upcoming release of GGIR, which will hopefully be online after the weekend, part 5 will not include SIB variables anymore as there is no scientific basis (yet) to support these and I realised that it is causing a lot of confusing when people are only interested in inactivity. In the upcoming release all part 4 and 5 variable names will be tidied up to be more intuitive. I am planning to circulate a summary of the main changes to GGIR next week.

The difference you found was because part 4 calcualtes these over the noon-noon window while part five focuses on the day (midnight-midnight) or waking-waking.
Thanks
Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Szymon,

Please see R package E4tools, which allows you to convert your E4 data to a csv format that can then be processed by GGIR with GGIR's read.myacc.csv functionality. It is a bit of a hack, but it makes it possible for GGIR to be used in a wide number of accelerometer brands providing that they can convert their data to csv.

If you have any feedback on the documentation then please let me know.
Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] discrepancy between bout.metric and boutcriter
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dominika,

Please note that part 2 uses arugments mvpadur and boutcriter, while part 5 uses argument boutdur.mvpa and boutcriter.mvpa. Make sure both of them are set.

Once these are set correctly the variable name in part 2 should update to the correct percentage.

I am aware that this is not very intuitive, but I have been hesitant to change argument names because that will impact on the re-usability. The price of facilitating consistency is that we are stuck with some ugly argument name choices. The same applies to some of the function names inside GGIR. At some point in the future I would like to do a clean up of the most confusing input argument names and function names, but at least not this year and not without consulting the user community.
Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR do.impute=1 questions
messages.body_plain:
GGIR imputes missing data (non-wear) with the average of the same time point on other days of the recording, but if the accelerometer was also not worn on those other days for that time point it imputes zeros. Variable "complete_24hcycle" in the csv report should give a quick impression of whether this was the case.

If you are interested in time series analysis without the help of GGIR then make sure you also export the non-wear detection to you understand where data was imputed. Note that the non-imputed epoch level data is available in the part 1 milestone data (folder: meta/basic)

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Dora,

I am afraid I have to disagree with you. Imputing with NA is the same as imputing by the mean of the remaining values. Especially for night time behavior that could be a problematic assumption. So, a real neutral imputation does not exist, even ignoring those data is effectively an imputation.

My advise would be to check the "complete_24hcycle" variable I mentioned. If this value is less than 1 and if the accelerometer has not been worn for at least a couple of days then do not use this recording in your analysis.

That said if you have ideas on how the imputation approach in GGIR can be improved then you are welcome to work on it and we can add it as an extra option for the user.

Best wishes,

Vincent

- GGIR’s package vignette now clarifies how to use published intensity cut-points from various data metrics, for hip and wrist-worn accelerometer data collected in a variety of age groups https://bit.ly/2xsrYzj <https://t.co/RnP0vnhjv3?amp=1>.

messages.subject: reading timezone and start time
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thank you for this excellent software! I'm new to the GGIR package, but have read through the tutorial, package documentation, and have searched the archives on this group. I am working with cwa data collected with AX3 axivity units and have 2 basic questions:

1) When using g.shell.GGIR(), the vignette tells me that "strategy" in combination with "hrs.del.start" and "hrs.del.end" can be used to subset incoming data by removing a certain number of hours from the beginning and end of the total file (the documentation describes it as how many hours after start of the experiment did wearing of the monitor start). In my experiment, however, I simply started the units some time in advance and noted the time at which wearing began. So in order to calculate the number of hours, I would have to extract the start time from the unit, calculate the number of hours between that time and when wearing started, and then enter that value here from processing. This can be done, but I feel like I must be missing an easier option to simply state the actual timestamp at which wearing started. Is this possible?

2) The first issue caused me to look into the function g.cwaread(), which I believe works under the hood for g.shell.GGIR. In this case, I can directly specify a start and end time point for reading data in "year-month-day hr:min:sec" format. This works, but I am having trouble understanding the function of the "desiredtz" argument in g.cwaread(). My data were collected in the UTC+08 timezone, and thus I do the following:

ac1 <- g.cwaread(fileName = "myfile.cwa",
          start = as.POSIXct("2020/03/02 17:00:00", tz= "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"),
          end = as.POSIXct("2020/03/05 08:20:00", tz="Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"))

However, I am surprised to see that this gives me a different output than if I specify desiredtz directly:

ac2 <- g.cwaread(fileName = "myfile.cwa",
          start = as.POSIXct("2020/03/02 17:00:00", tz= "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"),
          end = as.POSIXct("2020/03/05 08:20:00", tz="Asia/Kuala_Lumpur"), desiredtz = "Asia/Kuala_Lumpur")

I originally assumed that these would give me the same output because the devices were synced to this same timezone when they were configured and collected data. So it is unclear to me what exactly that argument is doing. The package documentation says to see g.getmeta() for details on this argument, but that only gives a link to a webpage with timezones. Could anyone comment on which of the above two approaches is appropriate?

Thank you!

Tom Kraft
Postdoc
UC Santa Barbara

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Problem with data files longer than 7 days
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

When doing analysis on days defined from midnight-to-midnight (MM) in GGIR part 5 days will by default only be included if they have at least 23 hours of data (any data, valid or not valid) which can be modified with argument minimum_MM_length.part5. This applies as of GGIR 2.0.

However, I personally think it is not a good idea to include incomplete days in part 5 MM analysis. Time-use in an incomplete day is not comparable to time-use in a complete data. So, person-level averages will be biased if you combine them. In other words it is not fair to compare the fact that I was inactive in half day recording with a day on which I had full data. The magnitude of acceleration imputation we use in GGIR data does not address this issue, because imputation is only useful for measures like average acceleration, not for time-use variables. We would need an imputation of the behavioral sequence to include those incomplete days. To my knowledge this does not exist yet. Anyone interested in working on this, please reach out to me. Further, if the recording starts and stops at a midnight the sleep estimates may not be reliable for the first half and last half night. Therefore, my advice would be: If you want to work with 7 MM days in part 5, collect at least an extra 8 hours of data before and after it.

Part 2, 4 and 5 will result in a different number of days/nights because each part has a different purpose. In part 2 we are not so much interested in time-use and more on average and distribution of acceleration, which are more compatible with the imputation we use. In part 4 we only care about whether sleep can be detected.  In part 5, both sleep and daytime time use estimates need to be complete for the majority of the time.

If you have suggestions on how we can better utilize those incomplete days of data then let me know. Otherwise I think the best advise is to aim for longer recordings than just the commonly used 7 days.

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
I think the quickest work around is to process the data with GGIR part 1 as you would normally do. Next, you will have to write an R script that does the following:
- Load the milestone (RData) files generated by GGIR part 1 as stored in the meta/basic folder.
- Create an extra timestamp column in object M$metalong by converting the timestamps to POSIX value with GGIR function iso8601chartime2POSIX.
- Change the non-wear score column in object M$metalong to 3 for all values outside your time interval of interest.
- Save all object you found in the milestone file back to the same file, including the now modified object M.
- Continue with part 2 with default settings for strategy. All time outside your value of interest will be treated as accelerometer non-wear time.

The other approaches you suggest are not going to work I think.

Good luck, Vincent

Hi Vincent,
Thank you for the very detailed explanation about the time-use analysis with GGIR. I totally agree with you that it is not a good idea to include any incomplete days (<24h in length) in the analysis. For our projects the wearing protocol is 8 days with the first and last day being only half-monitored and thus we only considered the 6 full 24-h days in middle for the MM window analysis.
However I noticed that in  both previous and current versions of GGIR, whenever I used the argument 'excludefirstlast.part5' in MM analysis, half of the estimated sleep duration for Day 2 (the first day of 24-h monitoring) was not included in the calculated sleep variables. It seems to me that this argument ignores the first half of sleep period (midnight to wake up of Day 2) of Day 2 in the part 5 analysis too. I was able to get the full sleep duration calculated for Day 2 in Part 5 when I set this argument as FALSE, though I would have to get rid of the first and last day of the data manually.

Best regards,

Kar-Hau, Chong (John)

On Mon, May 18, 2020 at 6:51 PM Vincent van Hees <v.va...@movementdata.nl> wrote:
> Hi John,
>
> When doing analysis on days defined from midnight-to-midnight (MM) in GGIR part 5 days will by default only be included if they have at least 23 hours of data (any data, valid or not valid) which can be modified with argument minimum_MM_length.part5. This applies as of GGIR 2.0.
>
> However, I personally think it is not a good idea to include incomplete days in part 5 MM analysis. Time-use in an incomplete day is not comparable to time-use in a complete data. So, person-level averages will be biased if you combine them. In other words it is not fair to compare the fact that I was inactive in half day recording with a day on which I had full data. The magnitude of acceleration imputation we use in GGIR data does not address this issue, because imputation is only useful for measures like average acceleration, not for time-use variables. We would need an imputation of the behavioral sequence to include those incomplete days. To my knowledge this does not exist yet. Anyone interested in working on this, please reach out to me. Further, if the recording starts and stops at a midnight the sleep estimates may not be reliable for the first half and last half night. Therefore, my advice would be: If you want to work with 7 MM days in part 5, collect at least an extra 8 hours of data before and after it.
>
> Part 2, 4 and 5 will result in a different number of days/nights because each part has a different purpose. In part 2 we are not so much interested in time-use and more on average and distribution of acceleration, which are more compatible with the imputation we use. In part 4 we only care about whether sleep can be detected.  In part 5, both sleep and daytime time use estimates need to be complete for the majority of the time.
>
> If you have suggestions on how we can better utilize those incomplete days of data then let me know. Otherwise I think the best advise is to aim for longer recordings than just the commonly used 7 days.
>
> Vincent
